note: Authored class-level rules with a source (I4). They apply only to the listed members and expand to exact pair keys (contracts.pair_key); nothing is inferred for a drug that is not listed. Aspirin is listed as an antiplatelet, not an NSAID, so no rule pairs it with itself. An explicit drug_drug entry for the same key wins.

rules.source: FDA NSAID class labeling, bleeding warning with antiplatelet drugs; ACC/AHA guidance after coronary stenting
rules.text: NSAIDs taken with antiplatelet drugs raise the risk of stomach and other bleeding. Worth asking the pharmacist about other pain-relief options.

rules.source: FDA NSAID class labeling and ACE inhibitor labeling: NSAIDs can reduce the blood-pressure effect and worsen kidney function
rules.text: NSAIDs can blunt ACE inhibitors and, together, strain the kidneys, more so when kidney function is already reduced. Worth raising with the pharmacist or prescriber.
